['The mountain is harsh and the water is harsh, words cannot be spoken, a deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river, and when I lose someone, I lose a part of myself too.  
When others lose someone, I lose someone as well. How could I not serve my husband faithfully despite this harsh fate?  
My poor husband, do not go—who will raise our young children? What sin do they bear in their youth? I just gaze up at the sky,  
thinking of my husband. When I think about it, I realized what my husband’s love truly was, but before I could fully understand, you passed away.  
How can I possibly raise this young, immature child alone? Ah, my grief…  
In this neighborhood alley, I wonder if my husband is here. Every day, whenever the sun rises, I think of my husband; even when looking at the moon, I think of him.  
I waited anxiously, hoping my husband would come home, but he has gone beyond this world. The cruel attachment remains even as I try to forget; no matter how much I steel my heart,  
your image from yesterday and today still appears vividly in my eyes.  
How could you leave me alone and go where you went?  
My in-laws complain morning and evening, my sister-in-law is troublesome, my brother-in-law is frantic,  
I carefully watch my behavior while trusting only my husband. With a single heart, I vowed to love you always,  
but why did you leave me and go beyond this world? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear.  
If I had known you were going to leave me, I would have built a fortress at the edge of the world where you went,  
If I had known it would come to this, I would have called a shaman to perform rites and exorcisms, to try to save you.  
I never imagined you would go beyond this world. They say that place beyond is better than this life; if I had known,  
every morning and evening I would have drawn holy water and prayed with my hands clasped, asking my husband not to die.  
Why did you leave me so heartlessly? Even today, I think of you. On the cold winds of winter’s end and the snow-filled solstice,  
the west winds of Bukcheongsan blow fiercely downward. That harsh winter has passed, and spring has come.  
The nightingale sings lightly and deeply, crying, and the mountains and trees—even dead wood—revive, sprouting leaves and flowers,  
but when will my departed husband come? Without a word, you torment me so.  
It is frustrating and painful; I cannot speak of it before me. A deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river.  
Coal, anthracite, bituminous coal, straw coal, bear’s fat—when burning, they produce smoke and steam, but my longing for my husband burns without any smoke or steam, only sorrow flows quietly like a droplet.  
Who understands this bruised liver? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, so dear, oh, my dear.', '1)

2)

-“Learned from watching a contest during Syngman Rhee’s era.”', 'Having committed an offense against the lord in the Moon Palace, the fairy was cast down to the human world.  
Coming down either underground or onto the land, she found there was nothing to do at all.  
Looking around the jade railing, she saw it was empty.  
Decaying within various mountains and hills,  
She hung the pumpkin vine and saw the four legs of a loom’s frame.  
These legs are the warp and weft legs,  
The front legs raised, the back legs lowered,  
After beating the reed, she placed it against the jade railing,  
Grasping the clouds and hanging the shuttle, setting the beat to sit,  
On top sits our honored lord, as if he were seated on a dragon throne.  
Draped in brocade, as if decaying in the thick mountain ranges with waist-hung mist,  
A proud figure appearing to be the only son of three generations,  
Whether famous or fortunate, appears adorned as well.  
Moving in and out like a bear in a bamboo grove, going in and out like a blackbird laying eggs in a gooseberry field,  
Playing in and out, back and forth.  
The one called the body household is our country’s magistrate’s wife,  
As if striking a hundred times.  
The three brothers tie strings to the eyebrows of a weeping face,  
Raising and lowering a count of millions of troops with a clamor.  
Climbing up and coming down with a clatter,  
Is it the fishing spear of the lonely fisherman oppressed by the widower?  
Floating on a river of clouds.  
The three brothers are the wild women dealing with grains,  
Surrounding the cloth seller and hanging a neck at the marketplace.  
Ascending and descending, the dragon head wails.  
In the deep mountain ranges, the wild geese have lost their mates and call to them along the path.  
The iron spirits of the temple city hang their necks like the local guardian,  
Seeming like a three-year-old child twitching its limbs,  
Coming and going.  
The flying sparrow is today the sound of thunder in a sudden rainstorm.  
The sewing frame is the magistrate of our country,  
Throwing their hoe as if striking here and there.  
Day by day, two days on end, weaving a piece of cloth.  
Making silver coins and twice emptying them, moving them here and there,  
Carrying woven threads,  
Washing in the front stream with rubbing and in the back stream with rinsing,  
Neatly finishing the blue thread, what cloth were they drying?  
They were drying the robes of a scholar who had passed the state examination.  
Lighting a fire in the weltercloth, setting it beside the dragon head,  
Lowering silk bedding, carefully sewing the robe.  
Slipping it slightly into the paulownia wood bundle,  
There's news that the scholar who passed the state exam is coming.  
Stepping outside the front gate, where is the frontline battalion?  
The royal guard stands in front, accompanied by thirty soldiers.  
Reporting the situation and returning,  
Ah, how frustrating is my fate! My miserable fate!  
At the prime of youth, with a healthy body, how could I live without fragrance?  
My dear, the scholar died of thirst—  
I'll give you water, so rise up!  
He died of hunger—  
I'll give you food, so rise up!  
Refusing both food and water, I want to go to Bukmang Mountain and the fields.  
Don't bury me on the front mountain nor the back mountain.  
Bury me right in the middle of the lotus pond.  
If light rain falls, pick lotus seeds and cover me.  
If thick rain falls, pick lotus flowers and cover me.  
If a heavy downpour comes, pick lotus leaves and cover me.  
The straight tree sways and falls down with a clatter.  

-From the folk song "Yangho"  
>']

Name: 1_sail_close_makes_husband
Representative_Docs:
['Sleep now peacefully, my dear little one  
Sleep, delight of my tender heart,  
Close, close your dear, your sweet little face.  
Sleep unhindered, free from pain,  
You are now in your most blessed place,  
Where you feel neither sorrow nor worry:  
No regret stirs in your little heart.  
Oh! May your state of bliss last forever!  
But, as the years grow, so will care and pain grow too,  
Sleep gently, sleep gently, my dear lamb,  
And may you be happy.

Sleep now peacefully, my dear little one,  
Sleep until the early morning stands.  
Close, close your dear, your sweet little face.  
Sleep is healthy for you.  
Oh dear delight! of your Mother;  
Oh little Angel, in whom appears  
The image of your good Father.  
My heart entrusts you to the Almighty Guardian!  
Grow up in all virtue, to honor the Fatherland.  
The state, the state, watches through time,  
And also relies on your hand.

Sleep now peacefully, my dear little one.  
And rest your little pure loan.  
You have already closed your sweet little face,  
Still unaware of the opposite.  
One can see in your charming being,  
Where in the sweet rose of Youth,  
That delights the Motherly heart,  
Is shown, calm peace read.  
Rest gently, my dear little Lamb, fulfill fulfill your desire.  
Sleep gently, sleep gently, your Mother  
Yearns beside you for rest.', 'Way: How sweet it is where friendship lives!

I rejoice in my blessed fate:
I have what I asked for;
Regarding rank and wealth, besides God,
No one ever has enough.
I have rest and daily sustenance,
No enemy brewing harm against me.
Whose welfare is the same as mine!

It is true, I work from early dawn
Until evening;
But the work makes me strong, healthy,
And also happily tired.
I am prepared to work,
And call idle laziness
A plague on Society.

What joy my soul feels,
When the work is finished;
Since I gain my merchant’s profit,
Who guards my well-being,
As he rewards me according to merit,
And shows himself a friend to mankind
Who fulfills his duty.

How then my wife and children rejoice,
When I return home.
Not one releases a single sigh:
Everyone praises the Lord Almighty,
Who brings people to our welfare,
And covers us with wings of love,
And clothes and feeds and drinks us.

I traded my humble state,
For no earthly riches:
Luxury and greedy excess
Give rise to poverty and sorrow;
But the labor that grants us benefit,
Elevates the heart that meditates in prayer,
On Him who governs all.

D.B.', "Listen, Friends and understand well,  
Hear this Song,  
Always abundant from the Fisherman,  
And also its use,  
For no City in the Netherlands  
Can do without it.  
There is scarcely a trade common,  
Large or small,  
That the Fisherman cannot see suffer,  
Few merchants praised,  
Unless goods from it  
Are found on the Ship.  
The Merchant ship brings Chalk and Grease,  
Also Pitch and Tar,  
Which the Fisherman first needs  
For his Ship without fail,  
Many a Skipper also goes away  
To fetch hemp.  
From this one makes Ropes and Cords  
Very abundantly,  
Many ships certainly sail to Spain,  
To get Salt from there,  
Wherewith he carries salt, Herring and Fish,  
Without fail,  
He addresses the Shipbuilder  
Before all men,  
Who makes his Ship masts well,  
To build for the Sea,  
Because he wants to complete his Journey  
With speed.  
The Smith generally makes Anchors,  
Builds large and small,  
The Block-maker also comes in handy,  
In various affairs,  
He must skillfully make Blocks, Pumps, and Compasses.  
The Line carriers also in the trade,  
Make many Ropes,  
And Cables for the Fisherman's Ship,  
So that it does not get caught  
In Storm and distress, on Sand or Rock,  
In these matters.  
The Sailmaker also makes  
His Sails ready;  
And the Cooper makes from split wood  
Large and small Barrels,  
In which he stores Herring and Fish in salt  
For his benefit.  
The Basket maker very pushy  
Makes from Rushes,  
Baskets, Traps, and good Holders,  
In which the Fisherman proudly  
Puts various fresh Fish,  
Skewers to keep alive.  
The Baker, Brewer, Grocer  
Know very well,  
That they have to do with the Fisherman,  
And the Shoemaker nicely  
Makes the Fisherman Clauses and Shoes,  
Worthy of praise.  
To the Cloth merchant in the season,  
He has much to do,  
Then the Tailor is addressed,  
Could I even imagine it all,  
How many a Workman  
Must earn his living.  
Few can harm the Fisherman,  
Even the Merchant,  
He buys Herring and Fish boldly,  
Sends them to various Countries,  
Then goods are obtained abundantly,  
In many ways.  
Also the Fisherman certainly brings you,  
Various kinds of Fish,  
With which many of their livelihood go,  
Skippers, Merchants, well-wishers,  
Simply the Fisherman is therefore loved  
By all People.  
He brings you the noble fine Herring,  
Cod done well,  
Halibut, Haddock, and Plaice,  
Whiting, Ling, Mackerel good,  
Also Turbot and Aberdeen,  
Abundantly.  
And still more other Fish,  
That is certain,  
The Fisherman brings you very boldly,  
To the Countryman's enjoyment,  
At his Table very abundantly,  
Good in flavor.  
Therefore do not despise the Fisherman,  
For much sorrow  
He suffers in Storms and distress,  
While the Countryman sleeps in peace,  
With his Wife and Children dear,  
As he wishes.  
See Friends this difference is great,  
Who can now earn his Bread  
Here on Land,  
Without having to sail out to Sea,  
Suffering the sorrow of Winter  
Storm and waves.  
Also he is often heavily burdened  
With a whole Journey,  
That he nevertheless enjoys no Profit,  
Yes whole Years,  
Tell me, is that not heavy sorrow,  
To sail like that.  
Mark once what gratitude you owe  
To God with diligence,  
Who lives here on Land in peace,  
Like blessed People,  
With Wife and Children to his liking  
And desire.  
Farewell Fishermen Young and Old,  
Trust in God;  
Even if you often have adversity,  
Do not therefore despair,  
You will gain Heaven's reward,  
But keep it.  
Who composed and established us this New Song,  
Was a good Fisherman from Vlaardingen,  
He was still Young in years,  
And wished the Fishermen much prosperity  
Who go to Sea."]

["In Vienna, in Vienna, oh yes, that beautiful city,
Which contains thousands of little soldiers,
There was a sweet girl who loved faithfully,
She had a little soldier as her best friend.
He went to desert to see his bride,
Because he knew very well it was not allowed.
They imprisoned him, oh what great sorrow,
His sentence was passed, oh yes it was: death!

The girl became furious, she immediately ran,
And threw herself on the ground before the Captain.
Oh sir Captain, free my little soldier,
Then you will make my heart joyful and happy again,
Oh sir Captain, I will give you some money,
If at least you care about that,
Oh my misfortune is great,
Spare my little soldier from the bitter death.

Your little soldier must die, that is the law,
That is what I have fixed now,
But I will give you three riddles,
If you know them, you save his life,
If you guess them, then he is saved,
If you listen to my words,
Otherwise it is over for him,
If you don't solve them, he must die.

Riddle. Tell me, does there exist a king without land?
Where is there water without sand?
What is more than all the money on earth?
What is worth millions to everyone?
How does one travel around the earth in a day?
Now, dear girl, tell me at once,
You save his life, I am listening,
Just guess it, otherwise it is over.

Oh save him then, I beg you sir.

Tell me what is worse than death?
Tell me who is the greatest power in every case?

Where is nothing that everyone must always have?
Be careful and guess this well again,
Oh German girl, his life depends on it,
Otherwise he undergoes his deserved punishment.

An evil woman who is worse than death,
God is the power, which does not please everyone,
The little fly forces itself everywhere.
One must have patience as long as one lives,
No one can exist without it.
My answer is now certainly right with that,
Oh sir captain! let my little soldier free.

He. Where is a mirror, girl, without glass?
What is most useful in the world?
Where is the key that fits all locks?
What can’t be grasped, even when you try hard?
What does man not lose before his death?
Guess these now, they are very great,
If you know them, he is free.
So be well and be joyful and happy.

She. The mirror of the heart has no glass,
Tolerance is the most useful,
Money certainly opens all locks,
The mist, I believe, cannot be grasped.
Hope leaves no one as long as he lives,
Now your word of honor that you give me,
Oh sir! I have now done my duty,
Let me now happily leave you.

Both. Well then, he has mercy, he is free.
Make yourself happy, joyful and glad;
We will now marry together,
And celebrate a happy wedding,
That is according to our wish and desire,
As a reward for our tender love,
Thus a clever girl saves her lover from death,
Is such love not truly great?", 'What one hears and sees today,
